title: From Gujarat to Georgia: How Nishant Shah Built a $200M Custom E-Commerce Empire
excerpt: Starting with a car wash and a frustration with print shops, the Gujarat-born, Georgia Tech-educated entrepreneur grew Group Bayport from a one-person signage startup into a 12-brand, 1,500-employee custom products company.
body:
• Nishant Shah, who moved from Gujarat to the U.S. for graduate school at Georgia Tech, has grown Group Bayport into a $200 million-plus custom e-commerce company headquartered in Atlanta
  • The company operates 12 brands — including BannerBuzz, Best of Signs, and Covers & All — offering over 10,000 customizable products across signage, home décor, outdoor furniture, and promotional materials
  • Group Bayport was entirely bootstrapped from a one-person startup in 2011 to $35 million in revenue by 2019, and has since scaled through organic growth and strategic acquisitions
  • The company now employs more than 1,500 people across the U.S., India, Canada, the U.K., and Australia, with a vertically integrated model spanning design, production, and fulfillment

When Nishant Shah was running a car wash business inside a U.S. mall, he kept running into the same problem: local print shops closed before his shift ended, and bulk order requirements made no sense for a small operation like his. That frustration — shared by thousands of small and medium businesses — became the seed for Group Bayport, now a $200 million-plus custom products company based in Atlanta, Georgia.

Shah, who grew up in Gujarat and came to the United States for graduate studies at the Georgia Institute of Technology before earning an MBA from Penn State, launched Caterpillar Signs in 2011 with a simple premise: let businesses design, order, and receive custom signage online, without minimum quantities or storefront hours. The company rebranded to BannerBuzz as it went global, entering the U.K. market and crossing $3 million in revenue by 2015.

From Signage Startup to Multi-Brand Empire

What began as an online sign shop has evolved into a diversified portfolio of 12 brands operating under the Group Bayport umbrella. BannerBuzz remains the flagship, offering premium custom signage worldwide, while Best of Signs caters to businesses needing 48-hour turnaround. Covers & All, now in its tenth year, specializes in custom-fit protective covers. Neon Earth sells personalized wall art and home décor. PatioHQ offers made-to-order patio furniture and cushions featuring performance fabrics.

"We believe that everyone has something to say, and the objects they choose should say it for them. Group Bayport allows people to reinforce their authentic self-expression through their surroundings."

— Nishant Shah, Founder & CEO, Group Bayport

The company's growth trajectory has been steep. Revenue stood at roughly $35 million in 2019, hit $120 million by 2022-2023, and now exceeds $200 million. Notably, the business was entirely bootstrapped through its first decade — Shah built the vertically integrated model, controlling the entire supply chain from marketing and web design through production and delivery, without outside funding.

Acquisitions Accelerate Growth

Group Bayport shifted to an acquisition strategy in 2019, purchasing Giant Media and Vivyx Printing to expand its signage and art printing capabilities. In 2024, it made two more significant moves: a full acquisition of Chicago-based NorthCape, a 25-year-old custom outdoor covers and furniture company, and a majority stake in Connecticut-based Optamark, a promotional products distributor with relationships with brands like Champion, The North Face, and New Balance.

"Delivering quality personalized products quickly and at value is what we do best," Shah said when announcing the 2024 acquisitions. "In adding these two strong category leaders to our portfolio, we offer our customers even more options to express themselves at home and at work."

A Vertically Integrated Model

Group Bayport's competitive edge lies in its vertically integrated structure. The company handles design, production, and fulfillment in-house, with a key production facility in Atlanta and centralized operations in India that serve as the backbone for all brands. This approach allows it to offer customization at scale — more than 10,000 products, serving over 10 million customers across North America, Europe, and Asia.

The workforce has grown to more than 1,500 employees spanning offices in the U.S., India, the U.K., Canada, and Australia. Shah's hybrid model — corporate and creative functions in Atlanta, production infrastructure split between the U.S. and India — enables the company to maintain competitive pricing while controlling quality.

Part of a Broader Trend

Shah's trajectory mirrors a broader pattern of Indian-origin entrepreneurs building significant American companies outside the traditional venture-backed tech startup model. Group Bayport is rare in the consumer e-commerce space for being both high-growth and consistently profitable, a distinction Shah attributes to the bootstrapped discipline of its early years and the vertical integration that followed.

"We manage the whole supply chain from marketing, website, and customer service to production. That's why we have a larger staff. We know what customers are looking for and where they are challenged."

— Nishant Shah, in a 2020 interview with Sramana Mitra

The company has expanded beyond the U.S. into Canada, the U.K., Australia, and New Zealand, with plans to continue scaling through both organic growth and further acquisitions in the personalized products space.
nri_angle: Gujarat-born founder exemplifies Indian-origin entrepreneurs building significant American companies outside Silicon Valley, with operations spanning the U.S. and India
author: Diaspora Desk
